label: Portrait character
summary: The character shown in a named portrait slot of the event window.
details: It takes the slot name as text, for example 'center_portrait' or 'right_portrait'. Vanilla uses the result as the data context of a portrait and passes it to the highlight check.

label: Portrait characters
summary: The list of all characters shown as portraits in the event window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the shared event window layout, so one entry is drawn per character.

label: Portrait name
summary: The name text shown for one portrait character of the event window.
details: Vanilla passes it a portrait character entry (EventWindowDataPortraitCharacter.Self) and uses the result as a text, so it gives the name shown for that portrait.

label: Event scope
summary: The script scope (the saved characters and objects) of the event shown in the window.
details: Vanilla chains it with scope lookups, for example reading a scheme saved under the name 'scheme' in the event, and then that scheme's task contract.

label: Letter signature
summary: The signature text of a letter event.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the letter event window. Going by its name and that use, it is the signature line of the letter.

label: Letter signed line
summary: The 'signed by' text of a letter event.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the letter event window, next to the signature. Going by its name and that use, it is the signing line of the letter.

label: Static portrait picture
summary: A portrait picture for a named portrait slot of the event window.
details: Vanilla gives it a slot name such as 'lower_left_portrait', a camera name ('camera_head') and the size of the widget, and uses the result as a portrait texture. Going by its name, the picture is a still one.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Name of a camera, as vanilla uses it.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: The widget's screen size, as vanilla uses it.

label: Theme header picture
summary: A picture of the event's theme, used as a header.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the character event window. Going by its name, it is the theme's header image.

label: Wide theme header
summary: A picture of the event's theme in a wide form, used as a header.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the big event window. Going by its name, it is the wide version of the theme header.

label: Theme icon
summary: A picture of the event's theme, used as an icon.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the activity window and in the big event window. Going by its name, it is the theme's icon.

label: Event title
summary: The title text of the event shown in the window.
details: Vanilla shows it in event windows and also in a localization text where it follows the activity's name in the activity window header.

label: Trigger breakdown
summary: A text that breaks down the event's trigger condition.
details: Vanilla shows it as a tooltip in the duel event window and in the shared event window layout. Going by its name and that use, it lists which parts of the trigger are met.

label: Has artifact
summary: Whether a named portrait slot of the event window shows an artifact.
details: Vanilla shows an artifact picture only when it is true, for the lower portrait slots.

label: Has artifacts
summary: Whether the event window shows any artifacts.
details: The input shows no vanilla use of this function on the event window. Going by its name, it is the general form of the check for one slot. The similar lines in vanilla belong to a character.

label: Has immediate effects
summary: Whether the event has effects that happen immediately when it opens.
details: The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it. This meaning rests on the name only.

label: Has opening
summary: Whether the event has an opening text.
details: Vanilla shows a part of the letter event window and of the anonymous letter event window only when it is true. Going by its name and that use, the opening is the first part of the letter.

label: Has portrait character
summary: Whether a named portrait slot of the event window holds a character.
details: Vanilla shows a portrait only when it is true, for slots such as 'left_portrait', 'center_portrait' and 'right_portrait'.

label: Has portrait characters
summary: Whether the event window shows any portrait characters.
details: Vanilla does not use it. This meaning rests on the name only.

label: Has portrait or artifact
summary: Whether a named slot of the event window shows a portrait or an artifact.
details: Vanilla uses it in a visibility condition, joining the checks for the lower left, lower center and lower right slots with Or.

label: Has portraits or artifacts
summary: Whether the event window shows any portraits or artifacts.
details: Vanilla does not use it. This meaning rests on the name only; it looks like the all-slots form of the single-slot check.

label: Has widgets
summary: Whether the event window has event widgets (extra interface parts inside an event).
details: Vanilla does not use it. This meaning rests on the name only.

label: Is character highlighted
summary: Whether the given character is highlighted in the event window.
details: Vanilla combines it with a hover check in a visibility condition: the part is shown when the portrait is hovered or this returns true. What makes the event highlight a character is not stated.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a character, for example from GetPortraitCharacter

label: Is showing transition
summary: Whether the event window is currently showing a transition.
details: Vanilla shows one layer of the shared event window when it is true, and another (the 2D effect layer) only when it is false. Going by its name and that use.

label: Is trigger fulfilled
summary: Whether the event's trigger condition is met.
details: Vanilla uses it in the duel event window and the shared event window layout to show one part when it is true and another when it is false. Going by its name, it reports the result of the trigger.

label: Event window data itself
summary: The event window data object itself, handed on as a value.
details: The game documents nothing more. Other types have a function of the same name and vanilla passes it as an argument, so this reading rests on the name.

label: Hide imprisonment
summary: Whether the imprisonment display should be hidden for a named portrait slot.
details: Vanilla shows something for imprisoned characters only when the character is imprisoned and this is false for the slot.

label: Show content source
summary: Whether the event window should show where the event's content comes from (such as a DLC).
details: Vanilla combines it with a check that the content source has an event decoration, and shows the decoration only if both are true.

label: Show portrait info
summary: Whether a named portrait slot should show its information tooltip.
details: Vanilla turns the tooltip on with it and lets mouse clicks pass through the portrait when it is false.

label: Show timeout info
summary: Whether the event window should show timeout information.
details: Vanilla uses it in the court events window to show a part of the window. Going by its name, that part concerns the time before the event times out.

label: Show debug option tooltips
summary: Whether the debug option tooltips are switched on.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a debug part of the royal court window and as a condition in the event windows when a fold-out is open. ToggleDebugOptionTooltips switches it. Going by its name, the tooltips are on event options.

label: Show event tools
summary: Whether the event tools panel (a developer aid for events) is switched on.
details: Vanilla uses it to show that panel in the royal court and shared event windows. ToggleEventTools switches it. Going by its name, it is a tool for testing events.

label: Theme starts with
summary: Whether the key of the event's theme starts with the given text.
details: Vanilla checks for 'travel' together with a valid travel plan of the player, to show a part of the character event window for travel events.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The text the theme key must start with.

label: Toggle debug tooltips
summary: Switches the debug option tooltips on or off.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click and when a letter window finishes. It returns nothing. Going by its name, the tooltips are on event options.

label: Toggle event tools
summary: Switches the event tools on or off.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the shared event window layout. It returns nothing. Going by its name, ShowEventTools reports the state.

label: Portrait character itself (access)
summary: The portrait character entry itself, the 'Access' variant of Self.
details: How it differs from Self is not documented. Vanilla does not use it on this type; other types have the same name. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Portrait animation
summary: The name of the animation the portrait character plays.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. Similar lines use a function of the same name on another type to pick an animation for an animated portrait. This reading rests on the name.

label: Portrait camera
summary: The camera used for the portrait character.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. Similar lines on another type pass a camera into an animated portrait. This reading rests on the name.

label: Portrait's character
summary: The character that the portrait entry shows.
details: Vanilla checks that the result is valid before showing the entry in the shared event window layout.

label: Portrait character itself
summary: The portrait character entry itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla passes it to other functions: to open the portrait tool of an entry and to get the name shown with it.

label: Portrait tool itself (access)
summary: The portrait tool object itself, the 'Access' variant of Self.
details: How it differs from Self is not documented. Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Animation search list
summary: The list of animations the portrait tool can search through and pick from.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a list in the shared event window layout. Going by its name, the tool is a developer aid for choosing portrait animations.

label: Camera search list
summary: The list of cameras the portrait tool can search through and pick from.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a list in the shared event window layout. Going by its name, it is the camera counterpart of the animation list.

label: Portrait tool itself
summary: The portrait tool object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Transition data itself (access)
summary: The event transition data object itself, the 'Access' variant of Self.
details: How it differs from Self is not documented. Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Transition picture
summary: The picture shown during an event transition.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the shared event window layout.

label: Transition video
summary: The video played during an event transition, given as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the video of a widget in the shared event window layout.

label: Transition video mask
summary: The mask video of an event transition, given as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the video of a widget in the shared event window layout, separate from the main video. Going by its name, the mask controls what part of the picture shows.

label: Has transition video
summary: Whether the transition has a video.
details: Vanilla uses it in three visibility conditions: alone, together with the mask check (video absent, mask present), and in a check that there is neither video nor mask.

label: Has transition video mask
summary: Whether the transition has a mask video.
details: Vanilla uses it in two visibility conditions: one for a mask without a video, and one for neither a video nor a mask.

label: Transition data itself
summary: The event transition data object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Window insert itself (access)
summary: The event window insert itself, the 'Access' variant of Self.
details: How it differs from Self is not documented. Other types have a function of the same name, and vanilla passes a widget's one to the activity window to get its event window insert. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Open event
summary: The event that is currently open in the window insert.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the event parts of the activity window.

label: Has open event
summary: Whether an event is currently open in the window insert.
details: Vanilla shows the event parts of the activity window only when it is true.

label: Mouse enters option
summary: Tells the window insert that the mouse moved onto an event option.
details: Vanilla calls it with the option under the mouse when the mouse enters it. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The event option the mouse entered.

label: Mouse leaves option
summary: Tells the window insert that the mouse left an event option.
details: Vanilla calls it when the mouse leaves an option in the activity window. It returns nothing.

label: Reload event window
summary: Reloads the event shown in the window insert.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click in the activity windows. It returns nothing. Going by its name, it redraws the event.

label: Window insert itself
summary: The event window insert itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Event widget itself (access)
summary: The event widget itself, the 'Access' variant of Self.
details: How it differs from Self is not documented. Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Widget event scope
summary: The script scope (saved characters and objects) of the event that the widget belongs to.
details: Vanilla reads saved values from it, such as a character saved as 'scope_character', or goes to the root character.

label: Event widget itself
summary: The event widget itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Chain progress widget itself (access)
summary: The event chain progress widget itself, the 'Access' variant of Self.
details: How it differs from Self is not documented. Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Chain progress entries
summary: The list of progress entries of an event chain, for the chain progress widget.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the list in the event chain progress widget, so one row is drawn per entry.

label: Chain widget event scope
summary: The script scope of the event that the chain progress widget belongs to.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. Other event widgets use the same function to read saved values. This reading rests on the name.

label: Chain progress widget itself
summary: The event chain progress widget itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Default text entries
summary: The list of ready-made texts the player can pick in the enter-text widget.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list and shows the list only if it has items.

label: Enter-text widget itself (access)
summary: The enter-text event widget itself, the 'Access' variant of Self.
details: How it differs from Self is not documented. Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Enter-text event scope
summary: The script scope of the event that the enter-text widget belongs to.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. Other event widgets use the same function to read saved values. This reading rests on the name.

label: Text edited
summary: Tells the enter-text widget that the player changed the text in its box.
details: Vanilla calls it from the text box's edit event. It returns nothing.

label: Enter-text widget itself
summary: The enter-text event widget itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Default entry itself (access)
summary: The ready-made text entry itself, the 'Access' variant of Self.
details: How it differs from Self is not documented. Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Default entry text
summary: The text of one ready-made entry of the enter-text widget.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a row in the list of default entries.

label: Is entry selected
summary: Whether this ready-made entry is the one currently selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed (down) state of the row's button.

label: Select entry
summary: Selects this ready-made entry.
details: Vanilla calls it when the player clicks the row. It returns nothing.

label: Default entry itself
summary: One ready-made text entry itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Naming widget itself (access)
summary: The naming event widget itself, the 'Access' variant of Self.
details: How it differs from Self is not documented. Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Character being named
summary: The character the naming widget is naming.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the child naming and the pope naming widgets.

label: Current name
summary: The name currently chosen or typed for the character.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the child and pope naming widgets.

label: Random ancestor name
summary: A random name taken from the character's ancestors.
details: Vanilla feeds it to the cultural name setter when the player clicks a button in the child naming widget. 'Available' and 'ancestor' are read from the name.

label: Random culture name
summary: A random name from the character's culture.
details: Vanilla feeds it to the name setter when the player clicks a button in the child and pope naming widgets. 'Available' and 'culture' are read from the name.

label: Random faith name
summary: A random name tied to the character's faith.
details: Vanilla feeds it to the cultural name setter from a button in the child naming widget. 'Available' and 'faith' are read from the name.

label: Random regnal name
summary: A random regnal name (the name a ruler takes on taking office).
details: Vanilla feeds it to the name setter from a button in the pope naming widget. 'Available' and 'regnal' are read from the name.

label: Naming widget event scope
summary: The script scope of the event that the naming widget belongs to.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. Other event widgets use the same function to read saved values. This reading rests on the name.

label: Name edited
summary: Tells the naming widget that the player changed the name in the text box.
details: Vanilla calls it from the text box's edit event in the child and pope naming widgets. It returns nothing.

label: Naming widget itself
summary: The naming event widget itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Set current name
summary: Sets the name chosen for the character to the given text.
details: Vanilla calls it from clicks, passing a random culture name or a random regnal name. It returns nothing.

label: Set current name (cultural)
summary: Sets the name chosen for the character, handling it as a name of their culture.
details: Vanilla passes it the first name base of the father, the mother or a grandfather, or a random ancestor or faith name, from clicks in the child naming widget. How it differs from SetCurrentName is not stated; going by its name, it applies the culture's naming rules.

label: Use regnal naming
summary: Switches the naming widget to regnal naming.
details: Vanilla calls it when the pope naming widget starts. It returns nothing. Going by its name, regnal naming means choosing a ruler's name on taking office.

label: Export tool itself (access)
summary: The export tool object itself, the 'Access' variant of Self.
details: How it differs from Self is not documented. Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Can export
summary: Whether the map editor's export tool can export right now.
details: Vanilla enables the Export button only while this is true.

label: Export tool cancel
summary: The action of the Cancel button of the map editor's export tool.
details: Vanilla runs it only from that button, which is disabled while an export is running, so it does not stop a running export. What it does otherwise is not shown, and the game documents nothing more. It returns nothing.

label: Export progress
summary: How far the running export has come, a decimal number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of the export's progress bar, whose end is MaxProgress.

label: Export progress text
summary: A text describing the current state of the running export.
details: Vanilla shows it only while an export is running.

label: Start export
summary: Creates an export file of the chosen workspace area of the map, using the selected mask.
details: Vanilla runs it from the export tool's Export button ("Create an Export File using this mask."), which is only active while CanExport is true. It returns nothing.

label: Heightmap picture
summary: The heightmap (the map's terrain height image) shown in the export tool's preview.
details: Vanilla draws it in grey in the zoomable preview, under the mask picture. The game lists no return type.

label: Mask effect
summary: A drawing effect that the export tool's preview applies to its mask picture.
details: Vanilla sets it on the picture drawn over the heightmap in the preview, whose shader is set by the game's code. What the effect does is not shown.

label: Export notes
summary: The notes text that goes with the export.
details: Vanilla shows it in the export tool's "Export Notes" box; editing the box sets it through SetExportNotes.

label: Selected mask
summary: Which entry of the export tool's mask list is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the selected entry of the "Select workspace area mask" dropdown. It returns a pair of whole numbers (a CVector2i).

label: Mask picture
summary: The picture the export tool draws over the heightmap in its preview.
details: Vanilla draws it with the mask effect on top of the heightmap, which suggests it shows the selected mask's area; the game documents nothing more and lists no return type.

label: Has masks
summary: Whether there are any masks (workspace areas) the export tool can export with.
details: Vanilla shows the export controls while it is true, and "There are no masks with which to export." while it is false.

label: Is exporting
summary: Whether an export is running right now.
details: While it is true, vanilla shows the progress bar and progress text and disables the Cancel button; otherwise it shows the zoom and pan hint.

label: Export progress end
summary: The value the export's progress reaches when it is done, a decimal number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the maximum of the export's progress bar.

label: Refresh export tool
summary: Refreshes the export tool's data.
details: Vanilla does not use it. This meaning rests on the name only.

label: Export tool itself
summary: The export tool object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Set export notes
summary: Takes the text typed into the "Export Notes" box as the export's notes.
details: Vanilla runs it when the user finishes editing the box; the box passes its text itself, so no argument is written. It returns nothing.

label: Select mask
summary: Selects the mask the user picked in the export tool's mask list.
details: Vanilla runs it when the selection of the "Select workspace area mask" dropdown changes; the dropdown passes the choice itself, so no argument is written. It returns nothing.

label: Eye dropper itself (access)
summary: The eye dropper tool itself, the 'Access' variant of Self.
details: How it differs from Self is not documented. Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Sample under mouse
summary: The terrain material sample at the map point under the mouse, as the eye dropper reads it.
details: Vanilla shows it in the map editor's eye dropper tooltip: the point's position and each material's share in percent. It returns a material sample.

label: Is eye dropper on
summary: Whether the map editor's eye dropper ("Inspect terrain materials under mouse pointer") is switched on.
details: Vanilla uses it as the button's checked state and shows the tooltip with the sample under the mouse only while it is true.

label: Packed value
summary: The eye dropper's list of packed samples, shown as "Packed values".
details: Vanilla builds one tile per entry under the "Packed values:" title, each with a material entry. The game lists no return type.

label: Packed dynamic value
summary: The eye dropper's list of dynamic packed samples, shown as "Packed dynamic".
details: Vanilla builds one tile per entry under the "Packed dynamic:" title, next to the packed values. How the two lists differ is not shown; going by the detail data panel, "dynamic" probably refers to the dynamic terrain materials feature. The game lists no return type.

label: Eye dropper itself
summary: The eye dropper tool itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Switch eye dropper
summary: Switches the map editor's eye dropper on or off.
details: Vanilla runs it from the eye dropper button with the opposite of IsEnabled, so each click flips it. It returns nothing.

fields.name: enabled
fields.text: Whether the eye dropper is on.

label: Packed sample itself (access)
summary: The packed eye dropper sample itself, the 'Access' variant of Self.
details: How it differs from Self is not documented. Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Sample channel
summary: The name of the channel this packed sample belongs to.
details: Vanilla does not use it. This meaning rests on the name only.

label: Sample entry
summary: The material entry stored in a packed sample of the eye dropper.
details: Vanilla uses it for each tile of the eye dropper's packed lists; a tile is active only when the entry's raw value is above 0. It returns a material entry.

label: Packed sample itself
summary: One packed eye dropper sample itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Faction itself (access)
summary: The faction itself, the 'Access' variant of Self.
details: How it differs from Self is not documented. Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Faction custom text
summary: Text from a custom localization (a named text template) run with the faction.
details: It takes the key of the custom text. The input shows no vanilla line on this type, but the name appears over 11,000 times with other types, where it is used this way. Going by that, the faction is the subject of the text.

label: Faction description
summary: The description text of the faction.
details: Vanilla shows it in the shared tooltip layout.

label: Faction discontent
summary: How discontent the faction is, as a number.
details: Vanilla does not use it. This meaning rests on the name and the number return type.

label: Faction icon
summary: The icon picture of the faction.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the factions window.

label: Faction leader
summary: The character who leads the faction.
details: Vanilla does not use it, but the return type is a character. Going by its name, it is the faction's leader.

label: Faction name
summary: The name of the faction, with a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in many texts, for example the title view and task contract descriptions. GetNameNoTooltip gives the plain name.

label: Faction name (plain)
summary: The name of the faction without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it as plain text in the shared tooltip layout and in many texts.

label: Faction power
summary: How strong the faction is, as a number.
details: Vanilla does not use it. This meaning rests on the name and the number return type.

label: Faction effect text
summary: A short text describing the faction's effect.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the factions window. Going by its name, it is a short description of what the faction does or demands.

label: Faction special character
summary: The special character of the faction.
details: Vanilla does not use it. The return type is a character; what makes one special is not stated, so this rests on the name.

label: Faction special character or leader
summary: The faction's special character, or its leader if it has none.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context for a character part of the factions window, shown when HasSpecialCharacterOrLeader is true. The fallback to the leader rests on the name.

label: Special character label
summary: The title text for the faction's special character.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the factions window. This meaning rests on the name and that use.

label: Faction special title
summary: The special title of the faction.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a title part in the factions window, shown only if HasSpecialTitle is true. What makes the title special is not stated.

label: Faction target
summary: The character the faction acts against.
details: Vanilla uses it in a tooltip text saying a member is already at war with the faction's target and will not take part if the demands are pressed.

label: Has special character
summary: Whether the faction has a special character.
details: Vanilla does not use it; it uses HasSpecialCharacterOrLeader instead. This meaning rests on the name.

label: Has special character or leader
summary: Whether the faction has a special character or a leader to show.
details: Vanilla uses it in the factions window to show the character part, and its opposite to show something else.

label: Has special title
summary: Whether the faction has a special title.
details: Vanilla combines it with ShouldShowSpecialTitle to decide if the title part of the factions window is shown.

label: Is at war
summary: Whether the faction is at war.
details: Vanilla shows the press-demands controls only when it is false and the player leads the faction. Going by that use, being at war means the faction's demands are already being fought for.

label: Is dangerous
summary: Whether the faction counts as dangerous.
details: Vanilla shows a part of the factions window when it is true and the player is not a member. What makes a faction dangerous is not stated.

label: Faction as scope
summary: The faction as a script scope, so that scope functions can be used on it.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla has no line on this type, but the same name is used over 1,000 times on other types. This reading rests on the name.

label: Faction itself
summary: The faction itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Show special title
summary: Whether the faction's special title should be shown.
details: Vanilla combines it with HasSpecialTitle in the factions window.

label: Character member itself (access)
summary: The faction's character member entry itself, the 'Access' variant of Self.
details: How it differs from Self is not documented. Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: Join score breakdown
summary: Text that lists the parts of the member's join score.
details: Vanilla uses it in the faction member tooltip, next to the commitment score. Going by its name, it explains how that score is made up.

label: Join score
summary: The member's commitment score to the faction.
details: Vanilla shows it in the faction member tooltip as the faction commitment, and notes that the member leaves if it falls below a limit set in the game's defines.

label: Member power
summary: How much military power this member contributes to the faction.
details: The member tooltip shows it as the member's military power contribution, and says the contribution is based on how many soldiers they have.

label: Member character
summary: The character who is the member.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a character and in a tooltip where a custom text is run on the member.

label: Is at war with target
summary: Whether the member is already at war with the faction's target.
details: Vanilla uses it to choose a line of the member tooltip text and as a visibility condition in the factions window.

label: Character member itself
summary: The faction's character member entry itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: County member itself (access)
summary: The faction's county member entry itself, the 'Access' variant of Self.
details: How it differs from Self is not documented. Vanilla does not use it on this type. This reading rests on the name only.

label: County join breakdown
summary: Text that lists the parts of the county's join score.
details: Vanilla uses it in the tooltip of a county (peasant) member of a faction. Going by its name, it explains how the score is made up.

label: County join score
summary: The county's commitment score to the faction.
details: Vanilla shows it in the county member tooltip and as a number in the factions window.

label: County power
summary: How much military power the county's peasants add to the faction.
details: Vanilla shows it in the county member tooltip as the faction military power contribution, which that text says is based on the county's levies and county opinion.
